overview: The file traces U.S. government consideration and implementation of revised telegraph and radiotelegraph rates between occupied Japan and the United States in 1947–1948. Federal Communications Commission correspondence first recommends postponing action on a rate change proposed by the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP) while the FCC investigates international communications charges, then acknowledges a SCAP proposal concerning country-to-country rates for Japan, Korea, and Okinawa modeled on the Bermuda Agreement. The final despatch reports a SCAP directive revising outbound Japanese radiotelegraph charges to equalize them with increased rates from the United States and Hawaii to Japan.

subfiles.title: FCC letter recommending deferral of SCAP telegraph-rate request
subfiles.from: T. J. Slowie, Secretary, Federal Communications Commission
subfiles.to: Francis Colt de Wolf, Chief, Telecommunications Division, Department of State
subfiles.about: The FCC recommends deferring action on SCAP's proposed change in telegraph rates between Japan and the United States pending a broader investigation of international communications charges.
subfiles.summary: Slowie responds to a February 21 letter that transmitted SCAP's proposed rate change for telegraphic messages between Japan and the United States. He explains that the FCC instituted an investigation of charges for communications between the United States and overseas and foreign points on March 12, with hearings scheduled to begin April 14. In light of that proceeding, he recommends postponing action on the SCAP request.

subfiles.title: FCC acknowledgment concerning rates for Japan, Korea, and Okinawa
subfiles.from: Paul A. Walker, Acting Chairman, Federal Communications Commission
subfiles.to: Walter A. Radius, Director, Office of Transport and Communications, Department of State
subfiles.about: The FCC acknowledges receipt of a SCAP despatch on telegraph rates and relates it to negotiations over country-to-country rates based on the Bermuda Agreement model.
subfiles.summary: Walker acknowledges Radius's November 17 letter transmitting an October 17 SCAP despatch about telegraph rates from Japan, Korea, and Okinawa. He states that the despatch appears to answer discussions initiated by the FCC in early September concerning country-to-country rates patterned after the Bermuda Agreement. The Commission is still considering the matter and promises a later reply.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 105 on equalization of radiotelegraph rates
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The Political Adviser's office transmits a SCAP directive revising radiotelegraph rates from Japan to the United States and Hawaii.
subfiles.summary: The despatch reports the enclosure of five copies of SCAPIN 1228/8, issued February 6, 1948, notifying the Japanese Government of revised radiotelegraph charges. The revision was designed to match an increase in rates for messages traveling from the United States and Hawaii to Japan. An appended schedule reportedly listed the revised charges for different classes of messages, although that schedule is not reproduced in the supplied pages.

interest: The file provides a compact view of how communications policy in occupied Japan was coordinated among the State Department, the FCC, and SCAP. It documents the progression from delaying a bilateral rate proposal during a general FCC investigation, through consideration of a Bermuda Agreement-style framework covering Japan, Korea, and Okinawa, to the eventual equalization of radiotelegraph charges. It is especially useful for studying the economic administration of the occupation, the regulation of postwar international telecommunications, and the treatment of Japan, Korea, and Okinawa as related communications territories.
